name: Orthonormal discrete Hartley transform
definition: H_k=N^(−1/2) Σ_(n=0)^(N−1) x_n [cos(2πkn/N)+sin(2πkn/N)]; x_n=N^(−1/2) Σ_(k=0)^(N−1) H_k [cos(2πkn/N)+sin(2πkn/N)].
variables: N positive integer length; n,k indices; x real input and H real coefficients
assumptions: Finite real vector and symmetric normalization
limitations: Equivalent information to the real-input DFT; direct evaluation is quadratic; not a claim of faster runtime
computation: Evaluate the real kernel sums in O(N²) arithmetic; inverse uses the same normalized kernel. Alternatively recover from a consistently normalized real-input DFT.

source.citation: FFTW 3.3.11 documentation, The Discrete Hartley Transform, section 2.5.3. https://ns.fftw.org/doc/The-Discrete-Hartley-Transform.html

application: General real-valued orthogonal transformation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
incompatible_methods: Complex inputs for the stated real-output specification
mechanism_note: With unitary negative-exponent DFT F, H_k=Re(F_k)−Im(F_k) for real x; F_k=(H_k+H_(−k))/2+i(H_(−k)−H_k)/2 with indices modulo N. The symmetric real kernel is orthogonal and involutory under the stated normalization. A feature transformation, not another distinct Fourier algorithm.

name: Prime-field number theoretic transform
definition: For prime p and N dividing p−1, choose ω of exact order N in F_p; X_k=Σ_(n=0)^(N−1)x_n ω^(nk) mod p; x_n=N^(−1) Σ_(k=0)^(N−1)X_k ω^(−nk) mod p.
variables: p prime modulus; N positive integer length; ω primitive Nth root; N^(−1) modular inverse
assumptions: Finite-field inputs; N divides p−1; exact order N verified
limitations: Direct evaluation uses O(N²) field operations with precomputed powers; modular residues alone do not recover unrestricted integer coefficients; exact arithmetic and suitable modulus are required.
computation: Verify p prime, ω^N=1 and ω^(N/q)≠1 for each prime divisor q of N (empty set for N=1); evaluate modular sums directly and invert N modulo p. No fast implementation claimed.
application: General finite-field transformation; no forecasting benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Prime modulus, vector, root of exact order N
incompatible_methods: Arbitrary complex-valued inputs without a specified mapping
mechanism_note: The prime-field multiplicative group is cyclic of order p−1. Summing ω^(k(n−m)) over k yields N for n=m and zero otherwise by the geometric-series identity in the field; N is invertible since N divides p−1. A finite-field Fourier analogue with different scalar domain, classified as a feature transformation rather than a new fast algorithm.
